Cimicifuga (Sheng Ma)
Source: https://zhongyibaike.com/wiki/%E5%8D%87%E9%BA%BB
Name
Bugbane Rhizome (Shengma)
Zhou Shengma (Zhou Shengma), Zhou Ma (Zhou Ma), Chicken-bone Shengma (Ji Gu Sheng Ma), Ghost-face Shengma (Gui Lian Sheng Ma), Green Shengma (Lu Sheng Ma)
Cultivation and Processing of Bugbane Rhizome (Shengma)
Source
Derived from the rhizomes of Ranunculaceae family plants: Shengma (Shengma), Xing'an Shengma (Xing'an Shengma) and Large Three-leaf Shengma (Da San Ye Shengma). Harvested in spring and autumn by digging up; remove aerial stems and soil, sun-dry until the fibrous roots are dry, then singe with fire or strike out the fibrous roots using a bamboo basket, and sun-dry.
Morphology
1) Shengma (Shengma)
Also called Ma Niao Gan (Ma Niao Gan), Huo Tong Gan (Huo Tong Gan). Perennial herb. Rhizome irregularly nodular, with hollow stem scars, many and long fibrous roots. Stem erect, branched, 1–2 m high, sparsely covered with soft hairs. Leaves pinnately compound several times; petioles densely covered with soft hairs; leaflets ovate or lanceolate, 2–4 cm long, 1–2.5 cm wide, margins deeply serrate, green above, grey-green beneath, both surfaces with short soft hairs. Compound-paniculate inflorescences borne in leaf axils or at branch tips, narrow or sometimes expanded into large panicles; flowers bisexual; calyx 5, ovate, imbricate, 3-veined, white, ciliate; nectary leaves (staminodes) 2, apex 2-lobed, white; many stamens, filaments of unequal length, longer than calyx; carpels 2–5, glandular-hairy, many ovules. Siliqua oblong-elliptic, slightly flattened, apex with a small persistent style, slightly curved. Seeds 6–8. Flowering July–August. Fruiting September. Grows under forests and in grassy mountain slopes. Distributed in Yunnan, Guizhou, Sichuan, Hubei, Qinghai, Gansu, Shaanxi, Henan, Shanxi, Hebei, Inner Mongolia, Jiangsu and other areas.
2) Xing'an Shengma (Xing'an Shengma)
Also called Di Long Ya (Di Long Ya), Ku Long Ya Cai (Ku Long Ya Cai), Dahurian Shengma (Da Hu Er Sheng Ma), Ku Cai Yang (Ku Cai Yang), Ku Li Ya (Ku Li Ya), Ku Zhuang Cai (Ku Zhuang Cai). Perennial herb. Rhizome large, with obvious hollow stem scars and many fibrous roots. Stem erect, solitary, over 1 m tall, densely covered with soft hairs. Twice ternately compound leaves; lower stem leaves with long petioles, petioles hairy, central leaflet stalked, lateral leaflets usually sessile; leaflets ovate to orbicular-ovate, 5–11.5 cm long, central leaflet again 3-lobed deeply or shallowly, margins deeply serrate, both surfaces hairy. Paniculiform compound inflorescence; main peduncle very long, lateral pedicels shorter, flower pedicels 2–4 mm long, all densely covered with gray soft hairs; flowers unisexual, dioecious, rarely bisexual; small bract beneath each flower; male flower calyx 5, obovate, 3-veined; nectary leaves 2, apically deeply 2-lobed, each lobe often with one distinct anther-like appendage; stamens numerous, filaments unequal, slightly flattened, anthers ovoid; ovary degenerate; female flowers with 5 carpels, sessile. Siliqua 5. Seeds many. Flowering July–August. Fruiting September. Grows on hillsides and shaded places. Distributed in Heilongjiang, Jilin, Liaoning, Hebei, Hubei, Sichuan, Shanxi, Inner Mongolia and other areas.
3) Large Three-leaf Shengma (Da San Ye Shengma)
Perennial herb. Rhizome large, with rounded hollow stem scars and many fibrous roots. Stem erect, 1–1.5 m high, glabrous or sparsely soft-hairy. Twice ternately compound leaves, lower ones with long petioles; central leaflet petiole longer, lateral petiole shorter, both covered with white soft hairs; leaflets ovate to broadly ovate, 9–11 cm long, 5–9 cm wide, central leaflet again shallowly 3-lobed, margins with coarse serrations, both surfaces hairy; upper stem leaves smaller, petioles very short. Inflorescence compound-paniculate; main peduncle and pedicels covered with gray soft hairs; flowers bisexual; calyx 5, broadly ovate, caducous; nectary leaf oblong-ovate with a nectar gland at the tip, yellowish-white; many stamens, filaments unequal, slightly flattened, anthers ovoid and 2-celled; carpels 3–5, free, glabrous, with short stalks, many ovules, short style, small stigma. Siliqua 3–5, apex with small persistent style, glabrous. Flowering July–August. Fruiting August–September. Grows in mountain fields and beside streams. Distributed in Heilongjiang, Jilin, Liaoning and other areas.
Properties and Flavor
Sweet, acrid, slightly bitter, cold.
Processing
Remove impurities, briefly soak and wash clean, lift out, moisten thoroughly, slice, and sun-dry.
Effects of Bugbane Rhizome (Shengma)
Efficacy
The rhizome of Ranunculaceae family plants Shengma (Shengma), Xing'an Shengma (Xing'an Shengma) and Large Three-leaf Shengma (Da San Ye Shengma).
Main indications: epidemic febrile pestilence, headache with chills and fever, sore throat, oral ulcers, rashes that do not fully erupt; sinking of middle qi, chronic diarrhea and dysentery, rectal prolapse, uterine bleeding and leukorrhea in women, uterine prolapse; carbuncles, swellings and sores with toxic pus.
Channels entered
Enters the Lung meridian, Spleen meridian, Stomach meridian.
Actions and indications
Raises yang, releases the exterior, disperses rashes, detoxifies. Treats epidemic febrile pestilence, headache with chills and fever, sore throat, oral ulcers, rashes that do not fully erupt; sinking of middle qi, chronic diarrhea and dysentery, rectal prolapse, uterine bleeding and leukorrhea in women, uterine prolapse; carbuncles and sores with toxic swelling.
1) Shennong's Materia Medica (Benjing): treats and resolves all toxins, repels warm diseases and obstructive evils (also called miasma or pernicious qi).
2) Bie Lu (Bielu): treats middle-region abdominal pain and nausea, epidemic toxic pestilence, headache with chills and fever, wind-swelling toxins, sore throat, oral ulcers.
3) Yaoxing Lun (Treatise on Medicinal Properties): treats pediatric wind and convulsions, epidemic febrile disorders. Can treat swollen and painful mouth and lips from wind-damp, rotten smelly tooth roots with heat toxin and pus and blood. Clears wind-heat obstruction in the heart and lungs preventing circulation, oral ulcers, vexation and oppression. Treats carbuncles, pea-sized sores; soak a cotton swab in the decoction and apply to the sore.
4) Rihuazi Materia Medica: calms the soul and settles the spirit, treats wandering wind-swelling toxins, latent halitosis and hidden lesions.
5) Tangye Materia Medica: in the “Main Therapeutic Secrets”: treats lung consumption with coughing of pus and blood, can induce superficial sweating.
6) Dian Nan Materia Medica: releases the exterior in pediatric measles and smallpox, resolves sore toxins, treats swollen throat, wheezing, hoarseness. Treats lung heat, relieves toothache. Treats breast thrush and mumps.
7) Compendium of Materia Medica (Bencao Gangmu): disperses rashes, regulates bleeding, treats yang collapse, vertigo and fainting, deficiency pain in chest and flanks, chronic diarrhea with heaviness, turbid leukorrhea, uterine hemorrhage, hematuria, uterine prolapse, impotence and cold feet.
Dosage and Administration
Internal use: decoction, 3–9 grams; or used in pills and powders.
External use: grind to powder for topical application, decoct for gargling or for washing.
Precautions and Contraindications
Contraindicated in cases of excess above and deficiency below, yin deficiency with vigorous fire, and in measles after the eruption.
1) Materia Medica Commentary (Bencao Jingshu): in cases of vomiting blood, epistaxis, cough with copious phlegm, yin deficiency with movement of fire, kidney deficiency, qi rebellion with vomiting, palpitations and fright, mania and epilepsy, avoid use.
2) Dipei Materia Medica: in early-stage cold damage of the Taiyang, when measles show superficial signs, with deficiency of the lower source (lower jiao), yin deficiency with fire blazing, these four conditions are contraindications.
Formulas Using Bugbane Rhizome (Shengma)
1) To treat cold damage, epidemic warm pestilence, pronounced wind-heat fever, headache, limb pain, early or unmanifested rashes:
Kudzu Root (Gegen) (scraped fine), Bugbane Rhizome (Shengma), White Peony Root (Baishao), Licorice (Gancao) (scraped, prepared) in equal parts. Grind coarsely. Each dose four qian, water one and a half bowls, decoct to one bowl, warm administer as needed. (From Yan’s Pediatric Formulas — Shengma Gegeng Decoction)
2) To treat pediatric smallpox, rashes unclear, fever and headache, wind-cold cough, breast thrush and mumps: Bugbane Rhizome (Shengma) 0.5 qian, Qianhu (Qianhu) 0.8 qian, Kudzu Root (Gegen) 0.5 qian, Baical Skullcap (Huangqin) 1 qian, Gardenia Fruit (Zhizi) 0.8 qian, fried Burdock Seed (Niubangzi) 1 qian, Licorice (Gancao) 0.3 qian, Platycodon Root (Jiegeng) 0.5 qian, Field Mint (Bohe) 0.5 qian, Chuanxiong Rhizome (Chuanxiong) 1 qian. Prepare with Dengxin decoction and administer. (From Dian Nan Materia Medica — Shengma Decoction)
3) To treat rapidly spreading eruptive disease on head, face and body that appears like fire sores with a white coating which opens and proliferates quickly (if not treated promptly, severe cases die within days; if poorly treated scars darken and persist for years — this is virulent toxic qi): boil Bugbane Rhizome (Shengma) in concentrated water, soak cotton and wash the sores. Bitter wine soak and boiling is preferable, but can cause severe painful dryness. (From Elbow Reserve Prescriptions)
4) To treat thunder-head wind, lumps and painful swellings on head and face with aversion to cold and strong fever, resembling cold damage: Bugbane Rhizome (Shengma), Atractylodes (Cangzhu) each 5 qian, one lotus leaf (Heye). Decoction and take. (From Medical Formula Explanations — Qingzhen Decoction, same as Suwen Bingji Baoming Ji Shengma Decoction)
5) To treat obstruction of the throat and blockage of fluids: Sichuan Bugbane (Chuan Shengma) half liang, Cirsium seed (Ma Jizi) one fen, White Alum (Bai Fan) one fen, Mirabilite (Mangxiao) one fen, Scrophularia (Xuanshen) one fen. Grind to powder and sieve, refine with honey into pills the size of a oleander seed. Wrap in thin cotton, keep a pill in the mouth to dissolve and swallow saliva. (From Shenghui Fang — Shengma Pill)
6) To treat acute painful throat obstruction: hold Bugbane Rhizome slices in the mouth until vomit occurs, or decoct half liang and take to induce vomiting. (From Renzhai Zhi Zhi Fang)
7) To treat yang-toxic disease with red mottled face like brocade, sore throat, expectoration of pus and blood (treatable within five days, untreatable after seven): Bugbane Rhizome (Shengma) two liang, Angelica Sinensis (Danggui) one liang, Sichuan pepper (flower) (Huajiao) one liang (stir-fried to remove sweat), Licorice (Gancao) two liang, Turtle Shell (Biejia) a piece the size of a finger (roasted), Realgar (Xionghuang) half liang (powdered). Combine six ingredients, water four sheng, boil down to one sheng, take at once; repeat for elderly and children until sweating occurs. (From Golden Cabinet Essentials — Shengma Biejia Decoction)
8) To treat mouth heat and sores: Bugbane Rhizome (Shengma) thirty zhu, Coptis (Huanglian) eighteen zhu. Powder the two and wrap in cotton to hold in mouth and swallow saliva. (From Qianjin Fang)
9) To treat gum detachment at the root, dental caries with swelling pain, loose teeth about to fall, failure of teeth to erupt, yellow teeth and halitosis: Notopterygium Root (Qianghuo) one liang, Gentiana (Longdancao) (washed with wine) one liang five qian, sheep tibia ash two liang, Bugbane Rhizome (Shengma) four liang. Grind finely, mix with very fine bone ash, make into a fine powder, apply to gums at night. (From Lanshi Secret Treasury — Tooth-holding Powder)
10) To treat stomach heat toothache: decoct Bugbane Rhizome (Shengma) and use the hot decoction to rinse the mouth and throat. (From Renzhai Zhi Zhi Fang)
11) To treat trismus and dysentery: Green Bugbane (stir-fried with vinegar) one qian, lotus seed kernel (remove heart, fry until dark yellow) thirty seeds, Ginseng three qian. Water one zhong, decoct to half a zhong and drink; mix with honey into pills for better effect, each pill four qian taken with warm plain water. (From Medical Broad Notes)
12) To treat uterine hemorrhage: Bugbane Rhizome (Shengma) five fen, Bupleurum (Chaihu) five fen, Chuanxiong Rhizome (Chuanxiong) one qian, Angelica Dahurica Root (Baizhi) one qian, Schizonepeta spike (Jingjie Sui) six qian, Angelica Sinensis (Danggui) six qian. Water two bowls, decoct to one bowl, take away from food and drink; usually stops within five or six doses. (From Mobao Zhai Collected Verified Formulas)
13) To treat retention of lochia or retained lochial material after childbirth for months up to one year: Bugbane Rhizome (Shengma) three liang. Boil with five sheng of clear wine to obtain two sheng, remove dregs, divide and take twice; will induce vomiting and purge retained material. (From Qianjin Fang)
14) To treat wind-heat in the heart causing widespread ulcerative lesions over the body: Bugbane Rhizome (Shengma), Rhubarb (Dahuang) (scraped and lightly fried), Baical Skullcap (Huangqin) (remove dark core), Immature Bitter Orange (Zhishi) (remove pulp and stir-fry with bran until yellow), White Peony (Baishao) each one liang; Licorice (Gancao) (prepared), Angelica Sinensis (Danggui) (cut and roasted) each half liang. Coarsely pound and sift; each dose five qian, water one and a half bowls, add a handful of lamp-wick fiber, decoct to one bowl, remove dregs, take on an empty stomach before evening meal. (From Shengji Zonglu — Shengma Decoction)
15) To treat sudden onset poisons with swelling and acute pain: grind Bugbane Rhizome (Shengma) with bitter wine and apply topically — effective. (From Buque Elbow Reserve)
16) To treat early-stage hard indurated carbuncles that are purple, with aversion to cold and high fever, not yet suppurated in one or two days: Bugbane Rhizome (Shengma), Forsythia (Lianqiao), Rhubarb (Dahuang) (scraped and fried), Rehmannia Root (Shengdihuang) (cut and roasted), Costus Root (Muxiang) each one liang, White Drum (?) (Bai Gu), Scrophularia (Xuanshen) each three fen. Pound coarsely and sieve. Each dose five qian, water two bowls, decoct to one bowl, add half qian of Mirabilite powder, remove dregs, take warm on empty stomach; administer until bowel function is achieved, repeat if no bowel movement. (From Shengji Zonglu — Shengma Decoction)
17) To treat pulmonary abscess with expectoration of pus and blood and foul odor, pain in chest and breasts: Sichuan Bugbane (Chuan Shengma), Platycodon Root (Jiegeng) (fried), Coix Seed (Yiyi Ren), Sanguisorba Root (Diyu), Baical Skullcap (Huangqin) (scraped), Moutan Bark (Mudanhpi), White Peony (Baishao) each half liang, Licorice (Gancao) three fen. Coarsely grate into a coarse powder, each dose one liang, water one and a half sheng, decoct to five he, remove dregs, take two to three times daily. (From Ben Shi Fang — Shengma Decoction)
18) To treat hot bi syndrome itching: decoct Bugbane Rhizome (Shengma) for internal use and wash externally. (From Qianjin Fang)
19) To treat seasonal epidemic warm pestilence, headache, fever, limb vexation and pain, rashes whether erupted or not: Bugbane Rhizome (Shengma), White Peony Root (Baishao), Licorice (Gancao) (prepared) each ten liang, Kudzu Root (Gegen) fifteen liang. Grind coarsely. Each dose two qian, water one and a half bowls, decoct to one medium bowl, remove dregs, take slightly warm at any time, three times daily until epidemic qi disperses and body cools; children take according to strength. (From Yan’s Pediatric Formulas — Shengma Gegeng Decoction)
20) To treat robust persons with heat toxin entering the stomach and intestines, joint and bone pain, abdominal vexation and fullness, constipation with dry stools: Bugbane Rhizome (Shengma), Rhubarb (Dahuang) (scraped and fried) each four liang, Qianhu (Qianhu) (remove sprouts), Gardenia Seed (Zhizi Ren) (fried) each three liang. Pound coarsely and sieve. Each dose three qian, water one bowl, decoct to seven fen, remove dregs and take warm before meals; repeat if not relieved. (From Shengji Zonglu — Shengma Decoction)
21) To treat cold damage after sweating, vomiting and purging, when toxic qi does not disperse and there is superficial deficiency with interior excess, heat manifests externally and the body is mottled like brocade, possibly with restlessness and delirium, also treating throat obstruction and swelling: Bugbane Rhizome (Shengma), Scrophularia (Xuanshen), Licorice (Gancao) (prepared) each half liang. Grind to the size of a hemp seed. Each dose about five qian, water one and a half bowls, decoct to seven fen, remove dregs and take. (From Lei Zheng Huoren Shu — Xuanshen Shengma Decoction)
22) To treat intermittent fever after cold damage with abnormal movements at irregular times: Sichuan Bugbane (Chuan Shengma) one to two liang, Hengshan (Hengshan) one liang, Shu lacquer (Shu Qi) one liang. Pound and sieve into powder. Each dose four qian, water one medium bowl, decoct to six fen, remove dregs and take warm on empty stomach; will cause vomiting after a long time, if not vomit repeat dose. (From Shenghui Fang)
23) To treat toothache and general head and facial heat from taking tonic herbs that produce stomach heat, with teeth sensitive to cold and aggravated by heat: Angelica Sinensis body (Danggui shen), Coptis (Huanglian), Rehmannia Root (Shengdihuang) (prepared with wine) each three fen, Moutan Bark five fen, Bugbane Rhizome (Shengma) one qian. Make into fine powder, one dose; water one and a half bowls, decoct to one bowl, remove dregs, wait to cool and take. (From Lanshi Secret Treasury — Clear Stomach Powder)
24) To treat oral ulcers: Bugbane Rhizome (Shengma), Phellodendron Bark (Huangbo), Indigo naturalis or a strong indigo (Daqing). Cut the three into slices, boil with water and use as a mouthwash, spit cold, symptoms improve. (From Waitai citing Jiyan Fang)
25) To treat dental wind exposing the root: Sichuan Bugbane (Chuan Shengma), White Aconite (Baifuzi) (processed and split) each one liang. Pound finely and sieve into powder, mix with raw Rehmannia juice, apply to the tooth root — immediate effect. (From Shenghui Fang — Sichuan Shengma Powder)
26) To treat sudden swelling and pain of the throat with inability to swallow saliva and to reduce heat and descend qi: fresh Ye Gan juice six he, Angelica Sinensis (Danggui) one liang, Bugbane Rhizome (Shengma) one liang, Licorice (Gancao) three fen. Sieve these four herbs, form into pills with the Ye Gan juice, wrap in cotton into the size of small beans, keep in mouth to dissolve and swallow juice three times daily and once at night. (From Yixin Fang quoting Zengshen Shengma Retaining Pill)
27) To treat throat pain due to accumulated wind-toxin in the viscera, where the toxic qi moves along the channels causing movable but fixed swellings in the body and pain in the throat; in pregnancy, urgent treatment is most appropriate otherwise both mother and child may be harmed, treat both before and after delivery: Bugbane Rhizome (Shengma), Platycodon Root (Jiegeng), Licorice (Gancao) each half liang. Grind and prepare into a powder. Each dose three qian, water one bowl, decoct to seven fen, take after meals. (From Puji Fang — Three-Combine Decoction)
28) To treat epidemic disease after which toxic qi attacks the eyes causing redness and ulceration: Bugbane Rhizome (Shengma) three fen, Cortex of Dictamnus (Qinpi) (remove coarse bark and scrape), Coptis (Huanglian) (remove fine roots), Solomon’s-seal Rhizome (Yuzhu)
One liang each. The above four ingredients are coarsely pounded and sieved, prepared for three uses; each time use one sheng of water, decoct to obtain half a sheng, filter through cotton to remove the dregs. Wash the eyes. (Sheng Ji Zong Lu: Eye-washing Cimicifuga (Sheng Ma) Decoction)
(29) Treats women's breast tubercles: Cimicifuga rhizome (Sheng Ma),
Licorice root (Gan Cao)
nodule,
Green tangerine peel (Qing Pi)
each two qian,
Trichosanthes seed (Gua Lou Zi)
three qian. Prepare as one dose; two zhong of water, decoct to one zhong, after meals sip it slowly. (Zheng Zhi Zhun Sheng)
(30) Treats postpartum retained bad matter not discharged, or after one month, half a year, or one year: Cimicifuga rhizome (Sheng Ma) three liang; with five sheng of clear wine, boil down to two sheng, divide and take warm again. If it induces vomiting and purging of the bad matter, do not be alarmed; it is good. (Qian Jin Yao Fang: Sheng Ma Decoction)
(31) Treats pediatric hematuria: Sichuan Cimicifuga (Chuan Sheng Ma) five fen, water five he, decoct to obtain one he, remove the dregs; a one-year-old child takes the entire dose in one day. (Gang Mu citing Yao Hezhong Pediatric Formulas)

Cinnamon twig (Gui Zhi)
Source: https://zhongyibaike.com/wiki/%E6%A1%82%E6%9E%9D
Name
Cassia Twig (Guizhi)
Liugui (Liugui)
Liugui (Liugui)
Sichuan Cassia Twig (Chuan Guizhi)
Cassia Twig Wood (Guizhi mu)
Cassia Twig Tip (Guizhi jian)
Guangmei Tip (Guangmeijian)
Cultivation and Processing of Cassia Twig (Guizhi)
Source
The young twigs of Cinnamomum cassia of the Lauraceae family; young twigs are cut between July and August, trimmed into small sections approximately 15 or 30–100 centimeters long, and sun-dried.
Taste and Properties
Pungent; sweet; warm in nature
Characteristics
Twigs are long and cylindrical, often branched, 30–70 cm long, with thick end diameters of 0.3–1 cm; surface brown or reddish-brown, with fine wrinkles and small tubercle-like leaf scars, branch scars and bud scars; lenticels are punctate or ovoid-punctate. Processed pieces are hard and brittle, easily broken; cross-section bark is reddish-brown, with a visible pale yellow ring of stone cells; wood is yellow-white to light yellow-brown; pith is slightly quadrangular. Possesses a characteristic aroma, tastes sweet with a slight pungency, the bark tasting stronger. The best material has young, thin, uniform twigs, reddish-brown color and a strong fragrance.
Effects of Cassia Twig (Guizhi)
Efficacy
The young twigs of Cinnamomum cassia of the Lauraceae family.
Main Indications
Wind-cold exterior syndromes; soreness and pain of shoulders, back and joints; chest impediment with phlegm-fluid; amenorrhea and abdominal masses.
Channels
Bladder channel; Heart channel; Lung channel
Indications
Induces sweating and relieves the muscles, warms the meridians and unblocks the channels. Treats wind-cold exterior syndrome, soreness and pain of shoulders, back and joints, chest impediment with phlegm-fluid, amenorrhea and abdominal masses.
1. Cheng Wuji: expels "bentun" (rushing abdominal pain), harmonizes the muscle exterior, disperses accumulated blood in the lower burner, and benefits lung qi.
2. From Yixue Qiyuan (Medical Origins), "Secret Therapeutic Methods": dispels wind-cold headache, opens the interstices, releases the exterior, and removes superficial wind-damp (the last two characters supplemented from Ben Cao Fa Hui).
3. Ben Cao Jing Shu: expels pathogenic factors from a replete exterior; mainly benefits liver and lung qi, headaches, and wind-bi with stiffness and pain of bones and joints.
4. Yao Pin Hua Yi: acts especially on the upper regions of shoulders and arms, able to lead medicine to painful areas to remove phlegm-congealed blood stagnation between the joints.
5. Ben Cao Bei Yao: warms the meridians and unblocks the vessels, induces sweating and relieves the muscles.
6. Ben Cao Zai Xin: warms the middle and moves blood, strengthens the spleen and dries dampness in the stomach, reduces swelling and promotes diuresis. Treats cold-induced numbness and soreness of hands and feet with tendon twitching and pain, as well as disorders from external cold.
Dosage and Administration
Internal use: decoction 1.5–6 g; in large doses can be used up to 15–30 g; or incorporated into pills or powders.
Precautions and Contraindications
Contraindicated in febrile diseases with high fever, yin deficiency with exuberant fire, and reckless movement of blood due to blood-heat.
Formulas Containing Cassia Twig (Guizhi)
1. For Taiyang windstroke with floating yang and weak yin—when yang floats the heat is spontaneously emitted, when yin is weak sweat issues spontaneously; chills with aversion to cold, gradually worse with wind, slight feverishness, nasal flaring and retching: Cassia Twig (Guizhi) 3 liang (peeled), White Peony (Baishao) 3 liang, Licorice (Gancao) 2 liang (honey-fried), Fresh Ginger (Shengjiang) 3 liang (sliced), Jujube (Dazao) 12 pieces (split). Finely cut the above five ingredients, use 7 sheng of water, simmer over low heat to obtain 3 sheng, remove dregs, take when warm, one sheng per dose; after taking, wait a short while and sip warm thin congee about one sheng to assist the medicine; cover warmly for about one hour; when the whole body is slightly moist as if sweating it is even better. (Shanghan Lun — Guizhi Tang)
2. For cold-induced disease on the eighth or ninth day with wind and dampness intermingled, body soreness and vexation, inability to turn over, no vomiting or thirst, floating, vacuous and choppy pulse: Cassia Twig (Guizhi) 4 liang (peeled), Prepared Aconite (Fuzi) 3 pieces (processed, peeled, cracked), Fresh Ginger (Shengjiang) 3 liang (sliced), Jujube (Dazao) 12 pieces (split), Licorice (Gancao) 2 liang (honey-fried). Use the above five ingredients with 6 sheng of water, boil down to 2 sheng, remove dregs, divide warm into three doses. (Shanghan Lun — Guizhi Fuzi Tang)
3. For pain of various joints, emaciation, swollen feet as if slipping off, dizziness and shortness of breath, nausea and an urge to vomit: Cassia Twig (Guizhi) 4 liang, White Peony (Baishao) 3 liang, Licorice (Gancao) 2 liang, Ephedra (Mahuang) 2 liang, Fresh Ginger (Shengjiang) 5 liang, Atractylodes (Baizhu) 5 liang, Anemarrhena (Zhimu) 4 liang, Saposhnikovia (Fangfeng) 4 liang, Prepared Aconite (Fuzi) 1 piece (processed). Use the above nine ingredients with 7 sheng of water, boil down to 2 sheng, take warm seven he (approximate measure), three times daily. (Jinkui Yaolue — Guizhi Baishao Zhimu Tang)
4. For chest oppression, various reversals, and heart-suspending pain: Cassia Twig (Guizhi) and Fresh Ginger (Shengjiang) each 3 liang, Immature Bitter Orange (Zhishi) 5 pieces. Use the above three ingredients with 6 sheng water, boil down to 3 sheng, divide warm into three doses. (Jinkui Yaolue — Guizhi Shengjiang Zhishi Tang)
5. For a person who after sweating for a cold feels palpitations below the navel and an urge to "run the piglet" (rushing abdominal pain): Poria (Fuling) half jin, Cassia Twig (Guizhi) 4 liang (peeled), Licorice (Gancao) 2 liang (honey-fried), Jujube (Dazao) 15 pieces (split). Use the above four ingredients with one dou of sweet water, first boil the poria until reduced by 2 sheng; add the other herbs and boil down to 3 sheng, remove dregs, take warm one sheng, three times daily. (Shanghan Lun — Fuling Guizhi Gancao Dazao Tang)
6. For blood-bi with both yin and yang deficient, slight pulses above the wrist and tightness at the middle of the forearm, external signs of body numbness like wind-bi: Astragalus (Huangqi) 3 liang, White Peony (Baishao) 3 liang, Cassia Twig (Guizhi) 3 liang, Fresh Ginger (Shengjiang) 6 liang, Jujube (Dazao) 12 pieces. Use the above five ingredients with 6 sheng water, boil down to 2 sheng, take warm seven he, three times daily. (Huangqi Guizhi Five-Substance Decoction)
7. For seminal emission with lower abdominal tension and cold at the glans, dizziness, falling away, very vacuous, faint pulses with slight tightness and movement of empty pulses indicating loss of essence and blood: Cassia Twig (Guizhi), White Peony (Baishao), Fresh Ginger (Shengjiang) each 3 liang, Licorice (Gancao) 2 liang, Jujube (Dazao) 12 pieces, Dragon Bone (Longgu) 3 liang, Oyster Shell (Muli) 3 liang. Use the above seven ingredients with 7 sheng water, boil down to 3 sheng, divide warm into three doses. (Guizhi Longgu Muli Tang)
8. For consumptive deficiency with interior palpitations and bleeding, abdominal pain, nocturnal emission, soreness and pain of the limbs, feverishness of hands and feet, dry throat and mouth: Cassia Twig (Guizhi) 3 liang (peeled), Licorice (Gancao) 2 liang (honey-fried), Jujube (Dazao) 12 pieces, White Peony (Baishao) 6 liang, Fresh Ginger (Shengjiang) 3 liang, maltose syrup one sheng. Use the above six ingredients with 7 sheng water, boil down to 3 sheng, remove dregs, add the maltose syrup and gently dissolve over low heat, take warm one sheng, three times daily. (Xiao Jian Zhong Tang)
9. For women with long-standing abdominal masses where menstruation stopped less than three months but continuous bleeding persists and fetal movement is felt above the navel—this is due to fixed masses damaging the pregnancy; for those who at six months of pregnancy feel movement above the navel, in the first three months bleeding during menses indicates a fetal condition. If bleeding does not stop, it is because the mass has not been resolved; the mass should be reduced: Cassia Twig (Guizhi), Poria (Fuling), Moutan Bark (Mudanpi) (pith removed), Peach Kernel (Taoren) (skin and tip removed and cooked), White Peony (Baishao) all in equal parts. Powder the five ingredients, bind with refined honey into pills the size of rabbit droppings. Take one pill before meals each day; if ineffective, increase to three pills. (Guizhi Fuling Wan; from Jinkui Yaolue)
10. For frostbite: Cassia Twig (Guizhi) 60 g, add 1000 ml water. Boil over high heat, after boiling continue for 10 minutes then remove; pour into a basin and wait until lukewarm (as tolerated by the patient and not scalding the skin), retain the residue for reuse with the next decoction. Immerse the affected limb in the decoction, wash while lightly massaging the lesion. Each immersion about 10–15 minutes, once in the morning and once in the evening. (Xin Zhong Yi supplement 1980, (3):16)
Dietary Therapy
Blood-Pressure-Elevating Tea (Shengya Cha)
Cinnamon Bark (Rougui), Cassia Twig (Guizhi), Honey-fried Licorice (Zhi Gancao) each 10 g. First grate the above three herbs into a coarse powder and set aside. Each time put an appropriate amount of the powdered herbs into a teapot, pour freshly boiled water and steep about 10 minutes, then drink as tea. Replace regular tea and drink frequently, continue for one week.
Effects: Strengthens heart yang, raises blood pressure. Indications: dizziness, mental fatigue, limb weakness, and low blood pressure below 90/60 mmHg due to heart yang deficiency.

Mussel-shell ash (bangke hui)
Cultivation and processing of powdered shell of freshwater mussel
Source
Made from the shells of Unionidae family mollusks such as the dorsal-horn toothless mussel, the corrugated crown mussel, or the triangular-sail mussel. The shells are washed clean, the black skin scraped off, and ground into powder or calcined to ash for use.
Properties and flavor
Salty, cold.
Effects of powdered shell of freshwater mussel
Functions
Made from the shells of Unionidae family mollusks such as the dorsal-horn toothless mussel, the corrugated crown mussel, or the triangular-sail mussel.
Transforms phlegm and reduces accumulations, clears heat and dries dampness. Treats cough due to phlegm-fluid retention, stomach pain, nausea and vomiting, leukorrhea, abscesses and swellings, and damp sores.
Channels entered
Enters the Lung, Liver, and Stomach channels.
Main indications
Transforms phlegm and reduces accumulations, clears heat and dries dampness. Treats cough due to phlegm-fluid retention, stomach pain, nausea and vomiting, leukorrhea, abscesses and swellings, and damp sores.
① Ben Cao Shiyi: Rotten shells powdered and taken internally treat nausea and phlegm-fluid accumulation in the chest.
② Ri Huazi Materia Medica: Treats gan (infantile malnutrition), stops dysentery and vomiting; for abscesses mix with vinegar and apply topically.
③ Compendium of Materia Medica (Bencao Gangmu): Relieves heat and dries dampness, transforms phlegm and reduces accumulation. Stops white turbidity and vaginal discharge, dysentery; removes damp swellings, treats water-related cough, improves the eyes, and treats genital sores, damp sores, and itchy carbuncles.
④ Yilin Zuanyao: Treats stubborn phlegm, stops coughing, clears the heart and preserves the lungs.
Dosage and administration
Internal use: used in pills and powders, 3–6 g.
External use: appropriate amount as a dry coarse powder; or mix into a paste and apply.
Formulas using powdered shell of freshwater mussel
① For phlegm-fluid cough: genuine powdered mussel (fried until red on a new tile), add
Indigo naturalis (qing dai)
a small amount, use dilute gruel water with a few drops of sesame oil, mix and take two qian (about 6 g). (Neijing Leibian Tested Effective Prescriptions)
② For accumulations of saliva-like masses lodged between the chest and abdomen causing stabbing chest and abdominal pain, long-standing and unhealed, or dry retching and reduced appetite: powdered mussel one liang (about 30 g),
Croton seed (ba dou)
seven seeds (remove shell and membrane). The above two ingredients are stir-fried together until red. If omitting the croton seed, instead form the powder into vinegar pills about the size of a wutong seed. For a man with umbilical and abdominal pain, fry with fennel and wine and swallow twenty pills; for a woman with blood and qi problems, fry with ginger and wine and take; for bleeding that rushes to the heart,
child's urine
and
Angelica sinensis (dang gui)
take with wine; for regular use take with ginger wine. (Shiyi Dexiao Fang — fried powder pills)
③ For abscesses and boils that are red, swollen and have a pointed head: mix with vinegar and apply mussel-and-clam ash; for dry cases it readily relieves them. (Prescriptions Worth a Thousand Gold)
④ For various sores and carbuncles:
Aconite (chuan wu)
, Powdered shell of freshwater mussel (bang fen),
Aconite (cao wu)
,
Hai jin sha (hai jin sha)
,
Adzuki bean (chi xiao dou)
,
Arisaema (tian nan xing)
each in equal parts. Grind into a powder, mix with
Rehmannia (sheng di huang)
juice and apply to the affected area. (Puji Fang: formula to reduce swelling and toxins)
⑤ For damp rot of the toes: rub on dry mussel-and-clam powder. (Shouyu Shen Fang)

Cultivation and Processing of Siberian Cocklebur Fruit (Cang Er Zi)
Source
Siberian Cocklebur Fruit is the mature involucre-bearing fruit of the Asteraceae plant Xanthium sibiricum Patr.; it is a toxic plant, the fruit being the most toxic, and use must strictly follow medical instructions.
Properties and Taste
Taste: bitter; sweet; acrid; nature: warm; slight toxicity
Processing
Remove all impurities, remove spines, sift off ash and debris, lightly stir-fry until yellow, remove and cool.
Description
Dried fruits with involucre present are spindle-shaped to elliptic, about 1–1.7 cm long and 4–7 mm in diameter; surface yellow-green, brown-green or dark brown, bearing numerous hooked spines about 2 mm long. One end has two relatively thicker sharp spines, separated or connected. The outer skin (involucre) is tough, internally divided into two chambers, each enclosing one small achene. The achene is slightly spindle-shaped, one side relatively flat; pericarp gray-black, papery, one end with a columnar base bearing a single spine-like projection; seed light gray, seed coat membranous, containing two cotyledons, embryo root located at the apex. Odor faint, taste slightly bitter, oily. Best quality is large, plump grains of yellow-green color.
Effects of Siberian Cocklebur Fruit (Cang Er Zi)
Efficacy
Siberian Cocklebur Fruit is the mature involucre-bearing fruit of the Xanthium plant in the Asteraceae family.
Indications
Dispels wind, relieves pain, removes dampness, kills parasites. Treats wind-cold headache, nasal obstruction with discharge (rhinitis/sinusitis), toothache, wind-cold-damp painful obstruction, limb contracture pain, scabies, pruritus.
Meridians
Enters
Lung channel;
Liver channel
Indications
Disperses wind, relieves pain, expels dampness, kills parasites. Treats wind-cold headache, nasal obstruction, toothache, wind-cold-damp painful obstruction, limb contracture pain, scabies, pruritus.
1. Ben Jing (Classic of Materia Medica): treats wind-head cold pain, wind-damp encircling obstruction, limb contracture pain, rotting flesh and dead muscle.
2. Ben Cao Shi Yi (Supplement to Materia Medica): soak in wine to dispel wind and tonify.
3. Ri Hua Zi Ben Cao (Rihuazi Materia Medica): treats all wind disorders, fills the marrow, warms the lower back and feet. Treats scrofula, scabies and itching.
4. Ben Cao Meng Quan (Materia Medica Primer): stops headache, unblocks the crown, chases wind toxin down to the bone marrow, kills childhood parasites hidden in dampness.
5. Ben Cao Zheng (Correct Materia Medica): treats nasal obstruction.
6. Ben Cao Bei Yao (Essentials of Materia Medica): good at inducing sweating, dispersing wind-damp, ascending to the brain vertex and descending to the knees, externally reaching the skin. Treats headache, dim vision, toothache, nasal obstruction, removes spines.
7. Yu Qiu Yao Jie (Pharmacological Explanations by Yu Qiu): reduces swelling and relieves obstruction, drains wind and eliminates dampness. Treats scabies, wind-itch and rashes.
8. Yao Yao Fen Ji (Essential Medicines Divisions): treats nasal breathing problems.
9. Hui Yue Yi Jing (Medical Mirror): treats various hemorrhoids.
10. Ben Cao Zai Xin (Materia Medica Revived): treats eye pain.
Usage and Dosage
Internal use: decoct as a decoction, 3–10 g; or used in pills or powders.
External use: appropriate amount, pound and apply; or decoct in water for washing.
Precautions and Contraindications
1. Do not use for headaches or bi pain due to blood deficiency.
2. Tang Ben Cao (Tang Materia Medica): avoid pork, horse meat, and rice-washing water.
3. Ben Cao Cong Xin (Materia Medica Renewed): disperses qi and consumes blood; people who are deficient should not take it.
Prescriptions using Siberian Cocklebur Fruit (Cang Er Zi)
1. For wind dizziness or severe headache: Siberian Cocklebur Seed (Cang Er Ren) 3 liang, Gastrodia (Tian Ma) 3 qian, White Chrysanthemum Flower (Bai Ju Hua) 3 qian. (Ben Cao Hui Yan)
2. To eliminate wind-damp bi and limb contracture: Siberian Cocklebur Fruit (Cang Er Zi) 3 liang. Pound to powder, use 1.5 sheng of water, decoct to obtain 7 he, remove dregs and sip. (Shi Yi Xin Jing)
3. Treat leprosy: Atractylodes Rhizome (Cang Zhu) 1 jin, Siberian Cocklebur Fruit (Cang Er Zi) 3 liang. Make each into powder, bind with cooked rice into pills about the size of a wuzi (Chinese parasol seed). Take three times daily, each dose 2 qian. Abstain from sexual activity for three months. (Dong Tian Ao Zhi)
4. Treat scabies, disperse wind and detoxify: stir-fry Siberian Cocklebur Fruit (Cang Er Zi) with clam meat and eat. (Sheng Cao Yao Xing Bei Yao)
5. Treat women’s wind-itch rashes and persistent pruritus: equal parts Siberian Cocklebur flower (Cang Er Hua), leaf (Cang Er Ye) and seed (Cang Er Zi), pound finely and sift into powder. Each dose 2 qian mixed with dou-lin wine. (Sheng Hui Fang)
6. For continuous purulent nasal discharge: Magnolia Bud (Xin Yi) 0.5 liang, Siberian Cocklebur Fruit (Cang Er Zi) 2.5 qian, Angelica Dahurica Root (Bai Zhi) 1 liang, Mint Leaves (Bo He Ye) 0.5 qian. Dry together in the sun and grind into a fine powder. Each dose 2 qian, take after eating with scallion and clear tea. (Ji Sheng Fang — Cang Er Powder)
7. For eye pain and tinnitus: Siberian Cocklebur Fruit (Cang Er Zi) half fen. Pound and mash, add 2 sheng of water, squeeze and filter to obtain juice, cook with 0.5 liang of polished rice into congee and eat, or make into powder or decoction to take orally. (Sheng Hui Fang — Cang Er Zi Congee)
8. For toothache: (a) Siberian Cocklebur Fruit (Cang Er Zi) 5 sheng, water 1 dou, boil down to 5 sheng, hold hot in the mouth; if painful spit out, then hold again. (Qian Jin Yi Fang)
8. For toothache: (b) Cocklebur Seed Kernel (Cang Er Ren), refined yellow and ground 60 g; Lophatherum Leaf (Dan Zhu Ye) (stems removed) 500 g; fresh ginger (Sheng Jiang) 120 g; edible white salt 180 g. In a small iron pot (clean), put in the bamboo leaves, add enough water to cover and boil over charcoal into a concentrated juice, then add ginger juice and boil, filter off dregs. Return the filtrate to the pot, boil and gradually add the white salt, stir and reduce to dryness, extinguish heat and remove the medicinal layer, mix with the ground Cocklebur Seed Kernel and grind into a fine powder, seal in a bottle for storage. When needed, take a small amount and apply to the affected tooth, rub three times daily until effective. (Shanghai Journal of Traditional Chinese Medicine 1983,(7):34 — Tooth Salt Powder)
9. For carbuncles and toxic swellings: Siberian Cocklebur Fruit (Cang Er Zi) 5 qian, lightly fry to powder and take with yellow wine; also apply egg white to the lesion to draw out the carbuncle root. (Experience Collection — Cang Er Wine)
10. For marked ascites and edema with scanty urination: equal parts Cang Er Zi ash and Ting Li Zi powder. Each dose 2 qian, taken with water, twice daily.
11. For wind throat blockage with deep swelling extending to the cheek and frequent belching, called "horse throat blockage": wrap three to seven pieces of Cang Er Zi in cloth and burn to ash, take with water. (Formulas 10–11 from Qian Jin Yao Fang)
12. For scrotal eczema: Siberian Cocklebur Fruit (Cang Er Zi), Cnidium Seed (She Chuang Zi), Licorice Root (Gan Cao) each 10 g. Add water and decoct to 1000 ml, externally wash the scrotum several times daily. (Compilation of Chinese Medicine Preparations)
13. For acute folliculitis and acute or chronic eczema: Siberian Cocklebur Fruit (Cang Er Zi) 120 g (crushed), Sophora Root (Ku Shen) 60 g, Wild Chrysanthemum Flower (Ye Ju Hua) 60 g. Decoction to 2000 ml and use to wash affected areas. For lichenified pruritic lesions, optionally add alum 30 g and Szechuan Lovage Rhizome (Chuan Xiong) 15 g. (External Materia Medica for Sores and Ulcers)
14. For chronic malaria that does not remit: Cang Er Zi and its root and stem may all be used. Scrape and crush into powder, mix with wine and cooked flour into pills, take when needed. (Zhu’s Collected Tested Prescriptions)
15. Treat hemorrhoids: take Cang Er Zi air-dried on the fifth day of the fifth lunar month, pound into powder, take one small spoonful by mouth three times daily until improvement. (Wai Tai citing 'Effective Prescriptions')
16. Treat lower limb ulcers: Cang Er Zi 60–120 g, fry until yellow and grind into powder, raw pork lard 120–240 g, mix and pound into a paste. Before use, clean the wound with lime water (500 g quicklime added to 8 kg boiling water, steep and stand 1 hour, decant the clear liquid), dry and apply the ointment, bandage externally. Change dressing every 5–7 days in winter, every 3 days in summer. (Jiangsu Traditional Chinese Medicine 1966(1):37)
Dietary Therapy Formula
Mint, Siberian Cocklebur, Magnolia Bud and Angelica Dahurica Tea
Mint (Bo He) 6 g, Siberian Cocklebur Fruit (Cang Er Zi) 12 g, Magnolia Bud (Xin Yi) 6 g, Angelica Dahurica Root (Bai Zhi) 6 g, scallion white (Cong Bai) 3 stalks, tea leaves 2 g. Put all the above ingredients into a pot, decoct with water, strain and collect the liquid. Use as a tea replacement.
Efficacy: disperses wind and opens the orifices. Indications: rhinitis, sinusitis and related conditions.
